result.instructions:
Pendenz is the private store of one person, the owner, for tasks, reminders and notes. workspace.actors names the owner (the actor of kind human). Write everything in the language the owner used for that item or note.
IDs: an item is shown to the owner as P-<id>, for example P-12. Tools accept P-12 or 12.
Before creating: search with list_items (q) for an open item that already covers it, and update that one instead.
Titles say the thing to do in plain words, as the owner would write it: "Call the dentist", "Renew the passport". Details, links and context go into the description.
Dates: due_at is either a day (2026-11-13) or a local time (2026-11-13T09:00). Times are local to the zone from workspace unless the owner names another place; then set due_tz. Never convert to UTC yourself. Work out "tomorrow" or "next Monday" from the current date in that zone.
Reminders: an item with a time in due_at reminds the owner at that time. Set remind_at only when the reminder should come at another time than the due time, or when a day-only item needs one. A day-only item without remind_at sends no reminder.
Repeats: repeat_rule needs due_at. A repeating item is one item: setting it to done moves it to its next date, leaves it open and unticks its checklist for the next round. Do not create one item per occurrence.
Status: todo, doing, done. Set doing when work on it has started, done when it is finished. Use add_comment for progress and results; anything still open belongs in the description or the checklist.
Comments: get_item lists them oldest first. A comment marked outdated: true no longer holds; do not rely on it. When a comment of yours stops being true, such as a plan that changed, mark it outdated with update_comment, and add a new comment for what holds now. You can change or delete only your own comments; delete one only when it was a mistake or the owner asks.
Agent stage: every item has an agent_stage. new means the owner added it, or changed its title or description, and it waits for triage; list_items with stage new finds those. An agent that triages sets it with update_item: none when there is nothing to do, otherwise gathering, needs_answer, ready and running as the work moves on, and declined when the owner said no. When the work is finished, set status done and agent_stage none in one update_item, with the result in a comment. Do not leave a finished item open for the owner to close.
Edits need the version from your last read. On a conflict read the item again and apply your change to the new state.
Projects group items and notes. An item without a project is in the inbox. Create, rename, re-icon or delete a project only when the owner asks for it. A deleted project does not come back.
Order: the inbox and each project have an order the owner sets by hand. list_items with sort manual shows it, with a position on every row, highest first. To move an item, set its position to a number between those of its two new neighbours, or above the highest to put it on top. Leave position alone otherwise.
Notes are plain markdown texts without a title field: the first line is the title. They hold context, not things to do; something to do is an item. Find notes with search_notes and read one with get_note before you rely on it. To add to a note use append_note, which cannot overwrite what the owner typed in the meantime. Use update_note with a new body only to rewrite a note, and only when the owner asks for it.
Writing a note: keep it very short. Plain text that reads well as typed, because the app does not render markdown: a title line, then short lines or "- " points. Only the facts the owner needs, no introduction, no summary, no headings, tables or bold.
Files: an item can carry files of any kind, pictures too, listed under files in get_item with an id, name, type and size; a picture also has a width and a height. Read or look at one with get_item_file when it matters for the task. Remove one only when the owner asks for it; a removed file does not come back.
Trash (trashed: true) is for mistakes and duplicates. Archive (archived: true) is for things the owner decided not to do. Neither is a way to finish an item.
Locked notes: a note whose text is private is locked, and the app then asks the owner for Face ID before it shows the text. You can still read it and add to it, and it is marked locked: true. Use its text only for the task you are on. Never save it or a summary of it to a memory, a journal or a log, never copy it into another note, an item, a comment or a message, and quote from it to the owner only as far as the task needs. search_notes shows a locked note by its title alone. Lock a note yourself (locked: true) when the owner asks for it or when you write something private into it, such as health, money or access details. Only the owner can remove a lock.
The owner can hide items and notes from agents. They do not appear here at all, so one that the owner mentions may be missing: say that you cannot see it instead of creating a copy.
Keys: give every write a key of your own that names the action, for example "tg-4812-create". If the call fails with a network error or times out, repeat it with the same key and the same arguments, so it cannot apply twice. A write without a key is a new action every time.

answer.description: Who you are, your scopes, the time zone for dates, all projects with their IDs and icons, and the allowed values. Call it once before your first write.
answer.name: workspace

answer.description: List items as compact rows (long descriptions are cut; use get_item for one item in full). Shows open items by default. Returns at most limit rows; when has_more is true, call again with a higher offset.

due_after.description: Day or local time, inclusive. With due_before: a date range.

due_before.description: Day or local time, exclusive. For "due today or overdue" send tomorrow's date here.

project.description: A project ID, or "inbox" for items without a project.

q.description: Text that the title or description contains.

sort.description: due = soonest first, undated last. manual = the order the owner set by hand in the inbox or a project; use it with project, and each row then carries its position.

stage.description: Agent stage. new = the owner added or edited it and it waits for triage.

answer.name: list_items

answer.description: One item in full: every field, its current version, its comments oldest first, and the latest changes (who changed which field from what to what). A comment with outdated: true no longer holds: do not rely on it.

activity.description: How many of the latest changes to include.

answer.name: get_item

answer.description: Add an item. Only the title is required; it lands in the inbox unless project_id is set. Check list_items first so you do not add a duplicate. Returns the new item as a compact row with its id and version.

checklist.description: Ordered steps inside the item. Replaces the whole list, so send every line you want to keep.

id.description: Keep the id of an existing line. Leave out for a new line.

due_at.description: A day (2026-11-13) or a local time (2026-11-13T09:00). Null clears it.

due_tz.description: IANA zone for due_at, such as Europe/Zurich. Leave out to use the zone from workspace.

position.description: Place in the manual order of its list, highest first. A number between the positions of the two neighbours it should sit between; read them with list_items and sort manual.

project_id.description: Project ID from workspace.projects. Null means the inbox.

remind_at.description: Local time of the reminder (2026-11-12T18:00) when it differs from due_at. Null clears it.

repeat_rule.description: FREQ=DAILY, WEEKLY, MONTHLY or YEARLY, optionally ;INTERVAL=2, ;BYDAY=MO,TH (weekly), ;BYMONTHDAY=31 (monthly). Needs due_at. Null stops the repeat.

source_url.description: The page or message the item came from. Do not invent one.

status.description: todo = not started, doing = in progress, done = finished.

tags.description: Lowercase words without spaces. Replaces the whole list.

key.description: A name you choose for this write, such as "tg-4812-create". Repeating the call with the same key and arguments returns the first result and writes nothing.

answer.name: create_item

answer.description: Change an item. Send its current version and only the fields that change. status done finishes it (a repeating item moves to its next date instead, stays open and gets its checklist unticked). archived or trashed move it out of the lists; false brings it back. Returns the item as a compact row with its new version.

agent_stage.description: Where the item is in the agent loop: none = nothing for an agent, gathering = collecting context, needs_answer = a question waits for the owner, ready = a brief waits for the owner's yes, running = the work is under way, declined = the owner said no. new means it waits for triage; the server sets it when the owner edits the title or the description.

tags.description: Lowercase words without spaces. Replaces the whole list.

key.description: A name you choose for this write, such as "tg-4812-create". Repeating the call with the same key and arguments returns the first result and writes nothing.

version.description: The version from your last read of this item.

answer.name: update_item

answer.description: Add a note to an item: progress, a result, a decision. When it no longer holds later, mark it outdated with update_comment.

key.description: A name you choose for this write, such as "tg-4812-create". Repeating the call with the same key and arguments returns the first result and writes nothing.

answer.name: add_comment

answer.description: Change a comment: a new text, or outdated: true when it no longer holds, such as a plan that changed. An outdated comment stays visible to the owner, dimmed. You can change only your own comments. Returns the comment with its new version.

comment.description: Comment ID from the item's comments in get_item.

key.description: A name you choose for this write, such as "tg-4812-create". Repeating the call with the same key and arguments returns the first result and writes nothing.

outdated.description: true when the comment no longer holds, false to take that back.

version.description: The comment's version from your last read of the item.

answer.name: update_comment

answer.description: Delete a comment, for one written by mistake or when the owner asks. This cannot be undone. When a comment is only out of date, mark it outdated with update_comment instead. You can delete only your own comments.

comment.description: Comment ID from the item's comments in get_item.

key.description: A name you choose for this write, such as "tg-4812-create". Repeating the call with the same key and arguments returns the first result and writes nothing.

answer.name: delete_comment

answer.description: Read one file attached to an item. A text file up to 1 MB comes back as text, a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP picture up to 5 MB as an image. Anything else comes back as its name, type and size only.

file.description: File ID from the item's files list in get_item.

answer.name: get_item_file

answer.description: Remove one file from an item, only when the owner asks for it. This cannot be undone. Returns the item as a compact row with its new version.

file.description: File ID from the item's files list in get_item.

key.description: A name you choose for this write, such as "tg-4812-create". Repeating the call with the same key and arguments returns the first result and writes nothing.

answer.name: remove_item_file

answer.description: Create a project, only when the owner asks for one. Check workspace.projects first. An icon that fits the name helps the owner find it. Returns the project with the ID to use as project_id.

icon.description: The symbol the app draws next to the project. "number" is the plain # every project starts with.

key.description: A name you choose for this write, such as "tg-4812-create". Repeating the call with the same key and arguments returns the first result and writes nothing.

answer.name: create_project

answer.description: Rename a project, change its icon, or both, only when the owner asks for it. The ID stays, so its items and notes keep their project. Returns the project.

icon.description: The symbol the app draws next to the project. "number" is the plain # every project starts with.

key.description: A name you choose for this write, such as "tg-4812-create". Repeating the call with the same key and arguments returns the first result and writes nothing.

answer.name: update_project

answer.description: Delete a project, only when the owner asks for this project to be deleted. Its items and notes stay and lose the project: the items are in the inbox afterwards. This cannot be undone, the project does not come back and its ID is not given out again. Returns the project with deleted: true.

key.description: A name you choose for this write, such as "tg-4812-create". Repeating the call with the same key and arguments returns the first result and writes nothing.

answer.name: delete_project

answer.description: List notes as compact rows: the first line as the title and the start of the rest (get_note for the full text). A locked note has locked: true and no preview. Pinned notes first, then the last edited. With q only notes whose text contains it. Returns at most limit rows; when has_more is true, call again with a higher offset.

project.description: A project ID, or "none" for notes without a project.

answer.description: One note in full, with its current version. A locked note comes with a notice on how its text may be used.
answer.name: get_note

answer.description: Add a note. Check search_notes first for a note that already covers the subject, and append to that one instead. Keep it very short and in plain text: a title line, then only the facts the owner needs. Returns the note as a compact row with its id and version.

key.description: A name you choose for this write, such as "tg-4812-create". Repeating the call with the same key and arguments returns the first result and writes nothing.

body.description: Markdown. The first line is the title.

locked.description: Locks the note: the app asks the owner for Face ID or Touch ID before it shows the text. For private text. Only the owner can remove a lock.

project_id.description: Project ID from workspace.projects. Null means no project.

answer.description: Change a note. Send its current version and only the fields that change. A body replaces the whole text, so read the note with get_note first; to add text use append_note. trashed moves it to the trash; false brings it back. locked: true locks it. Returns the note as a compact row with its new version.

key.description: A name you choose for this write, such as "tg-4812-create". Repeating the call with the same key and arguments returns the first result and writes nothing.

version.description: The version from your last read of this note.

answer.name: update_note

answer.description: Add text at the end of a note, on a new line. Needs no version: the text goes after whatever the note holds at that moment, so nothing the owner wrote meanwhile is lost. Returns the note as a compact row with its new version.

key.description: A name you choose for this write, such as "tg-4812-create". Repeating the call with the same key and arguments returns the first result and writes nothing.

text.description: Markdown. Start it with an empty line to set it apart from the text before.

answer.description: Everything that changed since a cursor: items, comments and projects in their current state, oldest change first. A project with deleted: true is gone, and its items are in the inbox. Store the returned cursor and send it next time. When reset is true, your cursor is no longer valid: start again from 0.

Never save it or a summary of it to a memory, a journal or a log, never copy it into another note, an item, a comment or a message, and quote from it to the owner only as far as the task needs. search_notes shows a locked note by its title alone. Lock a note yourself (locked: true) when the owner asks for it or when you write something private into it, such as health, money or access details. Only the owner can remove a lock.
The owner can hide items and notes from agents. They do not appear here at all, so one that the owner mentions may be missing: say that you cannot see it instead of creating a copy.
Keys: give every write a key of your own that names the action, for example "tg-4812-create". If the call fails with a network error or times out, repeat it with the same key and the same arguments, so it cannot apply twice. A write without a key is a new action every time.
